candidate.answerReason: Squaring twice shows that the displayed polynomial is \(((x-1)+1)^4=x^4\).

methods.label: Build the matching fourth power
methods.explanation:
Set \(t=x-1\), so that all five terms are powers of one quantity. To compare the expression with a fourth power, square \(t+1\) twice:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(t+1)^4
&=(t^2+2t+1)^2\\
&=t^4+4t^3+(4+2)t^2+4t+1.
\end{aligned}
\]
The coefficient \(6\) of \(t^2\) comes from \((2t)^2=4t^2\) and the cross products \(2(t^2)(1)=2t^2\). Thus this expansion matches the polynomial defining \(S\), giving
\[
S=(t+1)^4=((x-1)+1)^4=x^4.
\]
The answer is \(\mathrm{C}\).
